message.content:
Search this repository very thoroughly for the frontend API auth interceptor. Look for:
1. An HTTP/API interceptor that attaches auth tokens to requests (e.g., axios interceptor, fetch wrapper, or similar)
2. Files that manage authentication tokens (access tokens, refresh tokens, etc.)
3. Look in patterns like "interceptor", "authHeader", "Authorization", "bearer", "accessToken", "refreshToken" in frontend/web/app directories

Report the exact file paths, what tokens are managed (access token, refresh token, etc.), and how the interceptor works.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text: Now let me also look at the auth redirect utility and any other auth-related files.

Here is a complete report of the frontend API auth interceptor system in this repository.

---

## Core Files

### 1. Auth Interceptor -- `/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts`

This is the central file. It uses the **ConnectRPC** framework (not axios or raw fetch) with a typed `Interceptor` from `@connectrpc/connect`.

**How the interceptor works:**

- **`authInterceptor`** (line 156-178) wraps every outgoing RPC request:
  1. It calls `getRequestToken()` to obtain the current access token.
  2. It sets the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on the request via `setAuthorizationHeader()` (line 97-100).
  3. It sends the request via `next(req)`.
  4. If the request fails with a `ConnectError` of code `Unauthenticated` (i.e., a 401), and this is not already a retry attempt, it:
     - Calls `refreshAndGetAccessToken()` to refresh the token.
     - Sets the new token on the request header.
     - Marks the request with a custom `X-Retry: true` header to prevent infinite retry loops.
     - Retries the request once.
  5. If the retry also fails, it calls `redirectOnAuthFailure()` to redirect to the auth page, then rethrows the error.

- **Preflight token refresh** (line 124-150 in `getRequestToken()`): Before sending a request, if the token exists but is expired or about to expire (within a 30-second buffer), it proactively refreshes the token. This avoids sending expired tokens to public endpoints where a 401 would not be returned (and the server would just treat the request as anonymous).

- **Token refresh deduplication** (line 30-51): A `tokenRefreshManager` singleton ensures that if multiple requests trigger a token refresh simultaneously, only one actual refresh network call is made. All concurrent callers await the same promise.

- **Separate refresh transport** (line 65-72): Token refresh uses a dedicated `refreshTransport` without the auth interceptor, preventing infinite recursion when the refresh call itself needs to go out.

- **Service clients** (lines 192-203): All service clients (`memoServiceClient`, `authServiceClient`, `userServiceClient`, etc.) are created using the transport that includes `authInterceptor`, so every API call automatically gets the auth token.

### 2. Token State Management -- `/bench/repo/web/src/auth-state.ts`

This file manages a single token type: the **access token**. There is no refresh token stored on the client side (the refresh token is handled server-side via HTTP-only cookies, as evidenced by the `credentials: "include"` fetch option).

**Tokens managed:**
- **Access token** -- stored in both an in-memory variable (`accessToken`) and `localStorage` under the key `"memos_access_token"`.
- **Token expiry** -- stored in `localStorage` under the key `"memos_token_expires_at"` as an ISO date string.

**Key exports:**
- `getAccessToken()` -- returns the in-memory token, falling back to `localStorage`. Does NOT clear expired tokens from storage (to allow the refresh flow to attempt recovery).
- `setAccessToken(token, expiresAt)` -- sets both in-memory and `localStorage`, and broadcasts to other tabs via `BroadcastChannel`.
- `isTokenExpired(bufferMs)` -- checks if the token is expired or will expire within the given buffer.
- `hasStoredToken()` -- checks if any token exists in `localStorage` (even expired), used to decide whether to attempt refresh.
- `clearAccessToken()` -- removes the token from both memory and `localStorage`.

**Cross-tab synchronization:** A `BroadcastChannel` named `"memos_token_sync"` (line 13) is used so that when one tab refreshes the token, all other tabs immediately adopt the new token without making their own refresh requests.

**Expiry buffer constants:**
- `REQUEST_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS` = 30 seconds -- used for normal API request preflight checks.
- `FOCUS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS` = 2 minutes -- used for proactive refresh when the tab regains focus.

### 3. Proactive Token Refresh on Tab Focus -- `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useTokenRefreshOnFocus.ts`

A React hook that listens for `visibilitychange` events. When the tab becomes visible and the token is expired or expiring within 2 minutes, it proactively refreshes the token before React Query's `refetchOnWindowFocus` fires, preventing a burst of 401 errors.

### 4. Query Client Auth Integration -- `/bench/repo/web/src/lib/query-client.ts`

The React Query client is configured to **not retry** `Unauthenticated` errors (line 9-11), since the auth interceptor in `connect.ts` already handles token refresh and retry. If the interceptor still throws `Unauthenticated`, the session is truly invalid and the user will be redirected.

### 5. SSE Stream Auth -- `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`

The Server-Sent Events connection (line 202-211) also uses `Bearer` token auth. It calls `getRequestToken()` from `connect.ts` to get the token and sets `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` in the fetch headers. If the SSE endpoint returns 401, it calls `refreshAccessToken()` and retries the connection.

### 6. Auth Redirect -- `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/auth-redirect.ts`

Called when auth fails irrecoverably. It clears the access token via `clearAccessToken()` and redirects to the auth page, preserving the current URL as a redirect target.

### 7. OAuth Flow -- `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/oauth.ts` and `/bench/repo/web/src/pages/AuthCallback.tsx`

The OAuth callback page receives an authorization `code`, exchanges it via `authServiceClient.signIn()`, and stores the returned `accessToken` via `setAccessToken()`. The OAuth flow also supports PKCE (code verifier/challenge) when crypto.subtle is available.

---

## Summary

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Framework** | ConnectRPC (`@connectrpc/connect-web`), not axios |
| **Interceptor type** | ConnectRPC `Interceptor` in `/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts` |
| **Client-side tokens** | Access token only (stored in memory + `localStorage`) |
| **Refresh token** | Server-side only (via HTTP-only cookie, using `credentials: "include"`) |
| **Auth header format** | `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` |
| **Token refresh** | Calls `AuthService.refreshToken()` RPC; deduplicated via singleton manager |
| **Retry logic** | Single retry after 401 with refreshed token; marked with `X-Retry` header to prevent loops |
| **Failure behavior** | Redirect to `/auth` page with return URL preserved |
| **Cross-tab sync** | `BroadcastChannel` shares refreshed tokens across tabs |
| **Proactive refresh** | On tab focus (2-min buffer) and before each request (30-sec buffer) |
